diagnostic_interpretation: The initial probe filter matched zero tests because source preparation stopped before applying the probe. This is not semantic evidence. Probe2 records 45 raw original code64 observations on each core.

The first generated-model red included the original oracle handler HLT fetch Accessed effect at physical 0x13020. Final fixtures pre-access that handler page in both inputs so that model event-entry and original HLT observation have comparable output RAM. No output bytes are masked.

Isolated red2 uses the existing SelectorForRange profiles, and fails 36 saved exception-error-code comparisons on P4: nine instruction forms, two tail-crossing cases, two C routes. The E12 r6 run passes. The difference is at physical 0x1dfd0. These are preimplementation tests.
The first implementation green passes five groups with 360 original comparisons, 64 suspended comparisons and 16 full-mode comparisons per SDK. This is separate from final qualification.

Raw wrap and wrap2 stop with KVM_EXIT_FAIL_ENTRY (9) because the proposed loaded LDTR cache base itself is noncanonical. These are invalid-entry fixture failures, not guest instruction faults. The corrected wrap3 uses valid cached bases and records 72 original streams per core.

Raw wrap3 shows that an absent first descriptor page can have different ancestor Accessed effects on the two cores. The final matrix pre-accesses those ancestors in both inputs for this case only; it does not select or claim a new faulting-page-walk update policy. All final output RAM remains unmasked.

Expanded green2 passes five groups, 117 raw observations, 936 original/model comparisons, 64 suspended and 16 full-mode comparisons per SDK. Only diagnostic PML4/PTE address formatting changed afterward; earlier fixed diagnostic fields must not be interpreted as walk-path evidence for the expanded high/wrapped cases. Final clean-source qualification includes the corrected fields.

native_oracle.method: Fresh VM/vCPU per original stream; two initial SREGS writes, no intermediate host state rewrites. KVM_PRE_FAULT_MEMORY populates stage-2 backing. Original CPU and generated source start from the same CPU and guest RAM; compare full represented CPU state and all 0x40000 RAM bytes without output masks. The original handler HLT page is pre-accessed in both inputs. For the absent first wrapped descriptor page, its three ancestors are also pre-accessed in both inputs.

profiles.SelectorForRange: Observed E core type 0x20; code64 noncanonical descriptor start or tail raises #GP(selector).
profiles.SelectorForStart: Observed P core type 0x40; code64 noncanonical descriptor start raises #GP(selector), only tail raises #GP(0). Both profiles validate the full range before descriptor page-table access.

limitations: Observed target behavior is limited to these pinned local Intel hybrid cores; unknown core types are skipped. Production never infers a profile from its host.
KVM cannot admit the noncanonical cached-LDTR-base fixtures; no guest instruction result is inferred from those failed entries.
Protected ancestor Accessed inputs avoid an independently observed fault-walk difference; they do not qualify arbitrary initially-clear ancestor A behavior.

The read-only wrapped fragments prove write permission checks and first-PTE Dirty preservation. Their unchanged first-fragment descriptor bytes do not independently prove a partial descriptor-data store.
Software suspension comparisons test the retained software contract; original CPU runs are uninterrupted and do not expose intra-instruction hardware suspension.

coverage: Nine original forms: MOV FS register/memory, POP FS with 8/2-byte slots, LFS with 16/32/64-bit offsets, LGS32 and LSS32.

Thirteen cases: last low-canonical descriptor, noncanonical start, tail crossing with present/absent first translation, canonical high page fault, last high descriptor, end-to-zero qword wrap, absent first wrapped page, high-canonical valid descriptor, base-plus-index wrap, wrapped accessed update, either fragment write-protected.
Both HighC and LLVMC, host-x64 Clang/NeverC, O0/O2: 936 complete original CPU/RAM comparisons per SDK. CR2 begins nonzero; GP preserves it and PF records the exact first/second fragment address.

Explicit TailGPZero public profile variants map to the existing neutral descriptor canonicality authority. Legacy values retain their original semantics and numeric value; unknown public profiles fail before lower-owner effects.

Sixty-four paused comparisons retain the lower profile and full data/fault frame; ordinary contexts refuse either profile changing in both directions before effects. Sixteen full-mode comparisons use the originally frozen options even after reconstructing the outer context with opposite options.
Return/event constructors retain the established SelectorForRange choice; no new return/event target claim follows from selector-load probes.
boundaries: NeverC remains a host/source x64 compiler. Guest operand widths and NeverD guest modes do not add NeverC i386 support.

Full paged-source and legacy-source, shared event/native paging, instruction-boundary and SDK adapter checks are replayed. Prior broader lower-paging qualification remains separate and is not recounted.

Code64 return/event descriptor-tail qualification, remaining mode-aware owners, real/unreal/VM86 composition, software SMM/SGX, unbound asynchronous producers and physical SGX qualification remain open.
Production LLVM remains neverd-llvm-v23.0.0-r6. No LLVM release, production pin or source gitlink changes are included.
